identity.title: You Only Cache Once: Decoder-Decoder Architectures for Language Models

contributions.claim: Introduces YOCO, a decoder-decoder language-model architecture with a self-decoder encoding global KV caches and a cross-decoder reusing them through cross-attention.
Provides single-cache operation while retaining decoder-only Transformer behavior and global attention capability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish YOCO by caching key-value pairs only once, while its overall behavior remains like a decoder-only Transformer.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report favorable performance versus Transformer across settings that scale model size and training-token count.
The authors report near-perfect needle-retrieval accuracy at 1M context length.
Profiling reportedly shows orders-of-magnitude improvements in inference memory, prefill latency, and throughput across context lengths and model sizes.

narrative_sequence.summary: YOCO is introduced as a decoder-decoder architecture that caches KV pairs once.
A self-decoder encodes global KV caches, which a stacked cross-decoder reuses through cross-attention.
The model is described as behaving like a decoder-only Transformer while reducing GPU memory demands; its computation flow also permits prefilling to exit early without changing the final output.
The authors report favorable scaling comparisons, 1M-context needle retrieval, and orders-of-magnitude profiling gains in memory, latency, and throughput.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific architectural decomposition—global KV encoding plus cross-attention reuse—to both memory reduction and preserved global attention, and separately links computation flow to early-exit prefilling.

lessons.interpretation: Separating representation construction from later reuse can make a systems claim easier to explain by tying each benefit to a distinct mechanism.
lessons.application: When presenting an architecture, map each claimed efficiency benefit to the component or execution-path change intended to produce it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the abstract or paper cannot identify a plausible mechanism for each claimed benefit.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical values, experimental settings, baselines beyond Transformer, or definitions for “favorable,” “near-perfect,” and “orders of magnitude.”
The conditions and scope of early-exit prefilling, including how output equivalence is established, are unspecified.
